records.subject: spec-guard-codex-dispatch-rule
evidence: command:codex exec --json '按 AGENTS.md 的约定，实现 tasks/textkit/todo.md 中的全部任务（含 Checkpoint）。计划已获批准，不需要再确认。…' </dev/null

result:group A (tier-guard enabled) and group B (tier-guard disabled for that run with -c 'plugins."tier-guard@tier-guard".enabled=false') each issued exactly one spawn_agent per non-Checkpoint task (slugify, word_count)

result:in both groups the main agent committed and ticked Task 1 before spawning Task 2 (A 10:33:02 -> 10:33:24, B 10:38:54 -> 10:39:11, from rollout timestamps and git history); no child ran git commit; three commits each touching only that task's files; 8 tests pass; todo fully ticked

limit:Codex encrypts the dispatch payload (spawn_agent.message and the child's agent_message carry only encrypted_content), so whether the tier marker line was written into the prompt cannot be verified from host records; accepted by the user as a known limitation, criterion 2 applies to Claude Code only

limit:the workspace-write sandbox does not allow writing .git, so each git add/commit was requested with require_escalated and approved here by the configured guardian reviewer; an ordinary user sees an approval prompt
